::: {.hero-copy}
Power systems are easier to understand when physical intuition, mathematical models, and working examples are presented together. This site is an open collection of tutorials designed around that principle.

[Browse tutorials](tutorials.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg} [Contribute on GitHub](https://github.com/Plusero/powersys-foundation){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-lg}
:::

### Clear derivations

Follow each model from its assumptions to the final equation, with notation introduced where it is used.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Engineering intuition

Connect phasors, networks, machines, and controls to the physical behaviour they represent.

Turn theory into algorithms and numerical experiments that readers can inspect and extend.

## Start learning

The first worked tutorial introduces the nonlinear AC power-flow problem and derives the Newton--Raphson solution procedure.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" icon=false}
### Featured tutorial

[Newton--Raphson Power Flow: From Equations to an Algorithm](articles/newton-raphson-power-flow.qmd)

Derive the bus power-balance equations, assemble the Jacobian, and interpret the iteration as a sequence of local linear corrections.
:::

## Built in the open

Every article lives beside the site code in this repository. Readers can propose corrections, improve explanations, add examples, or contribute an entirely new tutorial through a GitHub pull request. See the [contribution guide](https://github.com/Plusero/powersys-foundation/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) to get started.
